lines.text: Valkey replaced a classic data structure and saved up to 43% of memory per item.
A skiplist puts each item in its own memory spot, linked by pointers. The new fbtree packs 61 items into one block.
lines.title: Skiplist vs fbtree

lines.text: Skiplist pointers cost about 37 bytes per item before storing the member name.
lines.title: The old cost

lines.text: Each skiplist step decides the next one, so the processor keeps waiting on slow memory.
lines.title: Why it is slow

lines.text: With 5 million members, overhead fell from 50.3 bytes to 28.5 with sequential inserts, and 32.0 with random ones.
lines.title: 5 million members

lines.text: Updating a score also got up to 105 percent faster in the team's benchmark.
lines.title: Speed

lines.text: Takeaway: nothing changes for users, except OBJECT ENCODING now says btree. Memory layout matters.
lines.title: Takeaway
